instruction.text: Select all the things that historians use to learn about the lives of the Maya.

feedback.end: A large amount of what we know about the ancient Maya today is thanks to the discovery of stone engravings and books that were produced during the height of their civilisation.
Codices were folded books made of bark paper and wrapped in jaguar skin. Only four of these have survived until today! They provide important information about the daily life of Maya society.

atoms.word: c o d i c e s

atoms.b: Inside the ((++codices leaflets)), there is evidence of the Maya ((++writing solar)) system in the form of hundreds of Maya hieroglyphs, or glyphs for short. The glyphs represent different sounds and words within the Mayan languages. They can also be found carved into stone ruins.

A group of signs that form a word or phrase is called a glyph block. The largest sign within a glyph block is called the ((++main little)) sign, while the smaller ones attached to it are called affixes.
By using columns of glyph blocks, the Maya were able to express complex ideas and stories, often related to important events or ((++astronomy astronauts)).

feedback.end: In Maya mythology, the serpent is a symbol of rebirth and transformation, linking to the shedding of their skin.
Sources suggest that Maya shields were made from wood and reeds.
Women were the traditional weavers within Maya communities and used natural dyes and cottons to create beautiful designs.
When night fell, the ancient Maya believed that the sun transformed into a jaguar. Jaguars were a symbol of strength and authority.
